channel.title: PSD Data Stories
channel.description: Source-led stories about public money and real outcomes.

item.title: The world is having fewer children. What changes next?
item.description: Follow 65 years of fertility and birth rates across 217 countries and territories—and what the transition means for families, schools and public budgets.

item.title: Europe puts a price on carbon. Where does the money go?
item.description: Follow an allowance from allocation to surrender, and auction revenue from buyers to public budgets and European funds.

item.title: Trade surged around Russia. Where did the goods go?
item.description: Follow suppliers, product baskets and onward exports through Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan—and test how much the trade statistics can establish.

item.title: The great oil pivot.
item.description: By 2025, China and India remain the major buyers of Russian crude in this comparison. Follow the shift from Europe on one globe.

item.title: Tariffs went up. Did America come out ahead?
item.description: Seven charts follow implemented tariffs, car imports, reciprocal duties and the cash the U.S. government actually kept.

item.title: The customs headline is not the cash kept.
item.description: Gross customs collections rose sharply. Refunds explain why net fiscal-year-to-date revenue tells a different story.

item.title: “Reciprocal” does not mean equal.
item.description: Look at the same car category in both directions: Canada, China, Europe and Mexico show very different tariff gaps.

item.title: Who keeps the digital economy?
item.description: Ten economies under the same assumptions: modelled leakage, domestic reinvestment and sensitivity without false precision.

item.title: Where did the money go? Czechia
item.description: Money supply, purchasing power and Czech National Bank interventions in one story.

item.title: Where did the money go? United States
item.description: Money supply, purchasing power and Federal Reserve interventions, in the same structure as the Czech report.
